original_method: Pin image digest and hpcg.sh; constrain reviewed host evidence directory; validate Docker/NVIDIA/driver/CUDA/MPI/transport privileges; map ranks to GPU UUID/BDF; preflight memory and problem semantics; resolve oracle; preserve baseline/isolate jobs; run four tracked containers sequentially; retain convergence/residual/performance/exit and files; stop containers, audit bind mount and compare health.

engineer_actions: Resolve architecture criterion and approve mount/mapping/oracle

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure executes NVIDIA GPU HPCG, while Criteria only references an undefined Intel/AMD spec with no compatible metric, topology or threshold.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; execution/result interpretation awaits project runtime and oracle inputs.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row281 Wistron-NV GPU-00274-V002: map or replace the Intel/AMD spec with an approved NVIDIA HPCG oracle for NP 1/2/4/8 at 256^3/rt2, including convergence/residual, performance/scaling, units/tolerances, rank-to-GPU mapping and controlled bind-mount boundary.

review_improvement: Preserves all four GPU HPCG runs, constrains host-file exposure and separates validity/scaling from an incompatible CPU reference.
independent_technical_reasoning: HPCG stresses sparse memory access and communication, so dense HPL or CPU vendor results are not transferable without a matched problem/runtime. Numerical convergence and residual validity precede performance. The writable bind mount crosses the container boundary and can change host files, requiring an isolated evidence directory and manifest alongside GPU/rank and memory preflight.
